verdict.rationale: dlt ships an official MCP server (dlt-mcp, server-card.json) explicitly described as 'exposing tools for inspecting, debugging, and managing dlt pipelines, secrets, schemas, and runs' (dlt-docs-72, dlt-probe-4), and dltHub's CLI/Web UI let users monitor pipeline health, inspect logs, and diagnose failures (dlt-docs-15), plus schedule/refresh/backfill/observe runs (dlt-docs-11, dlt-docs-78, dlt-docs-59/70). This covers status-check and diagnosis well and implies re-trigger via refresh/backfill, but there's no explicit documented MCP tool call or API endpoint named for 're-triggering a failed run' nor independent hands-on confirmation that an agent can actually perform this end-to-end. Missing for 10: explicit MCP tool/action for re-triggering a failed run, and independent/hands-on verification of the full check→diagnose→retrigger loop via API or MCP.
